blocks.text: Claudius. Named twice: a great famine, and Jews ordered out of Rome.
“Agabus "signified by the Spirit that there should be great dearth throughout all the world: which came to…”
ROME: 17 RULERS HEROD THE GREAT → PORCIUS FESTUS
Agabus "signified by the Spirit that there should be great dearth throughout all the world: which came to pass in the days of Claudius Cæsar." Acts 11:28
At Corinth Paul found Aquila and Priscilla, "lately come from Italy ... because that Claudius had commanded all Jews to depart from Rome". Acts 18:2
The city he ordered the Jews to leave
The disciples sent relief "every man according to his ability". Acts 11:29
Aquila, "born in Pontus", and his wife Priscilla were among the Jews who left Rome. Acts 18:2
Ag Agabus “there should be great dearth throughout all the world”
OUTSIDE THE BIBLE · REIGN OF CLAUDIUS, AD 41-54 (NO YEAR GIVEN)
OUTSIDE THE BIBLE · PLACED BY DIO EARLY IN THE REIGN
Dio Cassius on the Jews of Rome
His letter to Delphi naming Gallio
Began to reign 25 January AD 41 (Rolfe's note); died 13 October AD 54, 'in the sixty-fourth year of his age and the fourteenth of his reign' (Suetonius, Claudius 45).
E. H. Plumptre (Ellicott's commentary, about 1880); A. C. Hervey (Pulpit Commentary, 1884); R. J. Knowling (1900); J. C. Rolfe (1914); E. Schürer (1885) allows the inference

Chrestus is taken as Christus: the disturbances arose among Rome's Jews over preaching about Christ, like those Acts records at Antioch in Pisidia and Thessalonica. Rolfe calls Chrestus "another form of Christus" and thinks it probable that Suetonius erred in his chronology. Acts 18:2 Acts 13:50 Acts 17:5 [3][18][11][27][25]
H. A. W. Meyer (English translation 1877-80), after Wieseler and Ernesti

Meyer: "Chrestus was actually a current Greek and Roman name", so the phrase should be read as naming a Jewish agitator at Rome. Rolfe also leaves open that Suetonius means "some Jew of that name". Acts 18:2 [15][27]
Lumby sets out both readings and a third, a movement of Jews against Christians, and says "we cannot tell". Acts 18:2 [14]
Acts does not say why Claudius ordered the Jews out of Rome.
Acts does not say whether Aquila and Priscilla were already Christians when Paul met them.
Scripture says nothing of Claudius's death or of who followed him.

From the textActs names Claudius twice (Acts 11:28; 18:2). The site's person record also gives him "the decrees of Cæsar" at Thessalonica, which fall in his reign by date but name no emperor, and the "Caesar" of Paul's appeal in Acts 25-28. Acts 11:28 Acts 18:2 Acts 17:7 Acts 25:11
